### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/types`, touching **28** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/src/domains/own-door-bridge.ts`, `packages/types/src/server-fault-log.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via handleAIRequest (symbol, a top-level function), handleAutomationRequest (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/src/domains/own-door-bridge.ts`, `packages/types/src/server-fault-log.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **183** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0e361201b2a6062cccaa1a2f7d37b82b3ed0465a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d699696f2c4ad37c2ebd41e14800c1ced3f6c327` — the merge of head `76e31f9472599af796d16ef1e576bcb66df5eee7` into base `0e361201b2a6062cccaa1a2f7d37b82b3ed0465a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d699696f2c4ad37c2ebd41e14800c1ced3f6c327 && git checkout d699696f2c4ad37c2ebd41e14800c1ced3f6c327
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0e361201b2a6062cccaa1a2f7d37b82b3ed0465a 76e31f9472599af796d16ef1e576bcb66df5eee7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0e361201b2a6062cccaa1a2f7d37b82b3ed0465a && git merge --no-ff 76e31f9472599af796d16ef1e576bcb66df5eee7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0e361201b2a6062cccaa1a2f7d37b82b3ed0465a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0e361201b2a6062cccaa1a2f7d37b82b3ed0465a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d80d5fc3d7d49c3171d0c98159296276ab9fa74c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts + packages/runtime/src/domains/unavailable.ts, packages/runtime/src/endpoint-executor.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/own-door-bridge.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/domain-501-language-37811.test.ts (the pin the catalog docblock cites)

Read: card #37864 (body, triage, claim with the seat ruling "option B, discovery stays English", dev report, claim amendment), PR #38113 (body, 12-file list, net diff against merge base `93fa9118`), and the check-runs on this head. The rest of the diff (`ai.ts`, `automation.ts`, `notifications.ts`, `ui.ts` call sites, `catalog-activation-door.test.ts`, `endpoint-executor.test.ts`, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Check-runs at the time of this record: 24 success, 11 skipped, 31 still in progress, 0 failed. Concluded green: `Type Check · source gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, the five other finished `Lint ·` families, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Check PR Size`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`. NOT concluded: `Build Core`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Test Core` 1-10, `Test UI` 1-16, `Type Check UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`. This record judges the design; it does not stand in for those verdicts, and the queue reads them when they land.

### ① Derived judgments

- `BUILTIN_OPERATION_MESSAGES` gains five keys (`capability_unavailable_install`, `_unshipped`, `_ui`, `_ai`, `_search`) in all four locales: an additive accept-set change on a published constant. Right. No key is removed or renamed, and no other consumer enumerates the catalog's key set (grep at head: the keys are named only in the catalog, `unavailable.ts`, the two test files and the changeset).
- The five English templates against `serviceUnavailableMessage` / `REMEDY_DETAIL` (`core-services.zod.ts` at head), read character by character: `Install {{package}} to enable`, the unshipped sentence with `{{slot}}`, and the `ui`, `ai` and `search` sentences are byte-identical, the `search` one including its literal single-brace `{basePath}`, which `interpolateValidationMessage` (`/\{\{(\w+)\}\}/`) leaves alone. Right.
- Three zh-CN sentences change 「定制软件包」 to 「定制包」 (four occurrences; none left under `packages/` at head). The console bundles (`ui/packages/i18n` `zh-Hans.ts`, `studio/zh.ts`) say 「定制包」 throughout. Right; a wording change in one locale, no key or placeholder moves.
- Wire: the `/ai`, `/automation`, `/notifications`, `/ui` and custom flow-endpoint `501` gain `Vary: Accept-Language` on every answer, and a localized `error.message` only for a request whose top `Accept-Language` tag resolves to a catalog locale. Status, `error.code` and the English bytes are unchanged; no header and an uncatalogued language read the prior sentence. Right, and it matches the #37845 doors. No in-repo consumer string-matches these sentences.
- `capabilityUnavailable(deps, context, slot)` gains a required parameter. It is not exported from `@objectstack/runtime` (`exports` is `.` and `./compiled-plugin-manifest-file`; no index re-export), and all ten call sites are in the diff. Not a public-surface change. Right.
- Discovery (`services.SLOT.message`, `http-dispatcher.ts` and `protocol-discovery-and-bases.ts`) is untouched and still reads `serviceUnavailableMessage`. Right, per the ruling.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `37864-capability-unavailable-languages.md`: `@objectstack/runtime` patch, `@objectstack/spec` patch. Matches what the diff publishes: additive catalog keys, a translation wording fix, an added response header and a localized message on an unchanged status and code. Same level as #37845 for the same kind of change.

Clause-②: yes (widening) — on the PR body and the changeset, consistent with each other and with the diff (keys added, nothing taken away). `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: no file under `packages/metadata-protocol` is in the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the dev report. Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, surface amendment (`endpoint-executor.test.ts` added to the claimed files): covered by the seat's claim amendment on the card. Answered.
- Dev flag, `check:test-source-alias` exit 1 fixed in `9034ae85` by a module-top `@objectstack/metadata` import in the test: a test-only change, lane seat's remainder. Two derived gates reported NOT MEASURED locally (`check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`); their CI families (`Build Core`, repo and tooling lint) are among the runs not yet concluded above.
- `out_of_scope_findings: none`. Observation, not graded against this diff: fixed-English `501`s remain outside `src/domains/`, where the N4 walk does not look (`endpoint-executor.ts` `unsupportedAnswer`, `api-endpoint-step.ts`, `api-mapping.ts`, `action-execution.ts`, and the analytics `Install ... to enable the analytics API.` sentence in `dispatcher-plugin.ts`). They are not the `capabilityUnavailable` family and not on this card; the seat may want a follow-up card.
- SQL push-down: the diff touches no query, id materialisation or join. Nothing to flag.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts` — holds against the ruling and its first consumer. The docblock paragraph was read against the code it describes: the keys are read by the request's top `Accept-Language` tag through `catalogNotImplemented` with no `translate`, so no `errors.*` override is consulted ("read the same way" is true); `_ui`, `_ai`, `_search` are exactly `REMEDY_DETAIL`'s keys; every other slot takes `_install` or `_unshipped` on the same `CORE_SERVICE_PROVIDER` test and in the same precedence as `serviceUnavailableMessage`; and the pin it names exists and iterates every `CoreServiceName` plus an unknown slot. The new keys sit after `share_links_unconfigured` in every locale, so the earlier paragraph's "from `auth_service_unavailable` to `share_links_unconfigured`" range still describes what it described. Translations read correctly in zh-CN, ja-JP and es-ES; package, slot, plugin and route names are left untranslated as the docblock says, and placeholders match the English in each locale.

`packages/runtime/src/domains/unavailable.ts` — agrees with the contract sentence by sentence. `capabilityUnavailableSentence` mirrors `serviceUnavailableMessage` branch for branch; a slot later given a `REMEDY_DETAIL` sentence fails the pin until it is mapped, as the docblock claims. Tried: an unknown slot (English equal, pinned), a locale with a region the catalog lacks (`en-US`, pinned; `es-MX` resolves by language), a `{{` inside a slot value (single interpolation pass, printed as written).

`packages/runtime/src/endpoint-executor.ts` — both flow-target `501`s answer `automationUnavailableAnswer`. `ctx.protocolContext.request` is the raw request, whose `headers` record `requestLocaleOf` reads; the `headers` on the answer survive `api-endpoint-step.ts` (`...(answer.headers ?? {})`, applied on failure too), so the `Vary` reaches the writer.

`packages/runtime/src/domains/own-door-bridge.ts` — the `requestLocaleOf` jsdoc now names its two direct callers; both exist as described.

`domain-501-language-37811.test.ts` as the enforcing pin — the drift half does what the docblock says it does.

S1 (should-fix) — The operator's fault log now takes the first caller's language, and nothing in the diff says so. `dispatcher-plugin.ts` hands `body.error.message` of a composed 5xx to `logServerFault`, and a `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` is a declared capability absence (#14656): one `warn` line per route per process. With this change that one line for `/ai`, `/automation`, `/notifications` and `/ui` is the localized sentence, so whichever request reaches the route first after a restart fixes the language of the only line the operator gets (a zh-CN or ja-JP browser yields a Chinese or Japanese log line for the life of the process). `packages/types/src/server-fault-log.ts` names this exact producer and states that its `501` "carries `serviceUnavailableMessage(slot)`", which is no longer true for such a request. The #37845 doors already behave this way, but this is the family #14656 was ruled on and the high-traffic one (Studio polls `/ai` unprompted). The catalog docblock states the fault-log behaviour for the `print_*` keys and is silent here. Either keep the log line English (hand the funnel the English sentence while the wire carries the localized one), or rule the behaviour acceptable and say so in the catalog paragraph and `unavailable.ts`, correcting the `server-fault-log.ts` sentence with it.

N1 (nit) — `unavailable.ts` says the `501` follows the request's language "as every other domain 501 does"; the walk in this same PR lists two domain `501`s that deliberately do not (`meta.ts` `errorFromThrown`, `mcp.ts` `resumeDoorError`). "As the other catalog `501`s do" would be exact.

N2 (nit) — `codeOnly` does not lex regex literals: a quote or `//` inside one blanks the rest of that line, and a backtick inside one would blank to the next backtick. No domain module at head has such a regex (grep), and the exactly-one-site exemption tests would trip in three files, so nothing is hidden today; a `501` reached through a helper outside `src/domains/` is likewise not seen. A comment on the walker naming the two limits would do.

N3 (nit) — zh-CN says 「没有随附的实现」 in `_unshipped` and `_search` and 「不附带实现」 in `_ai` for the same English verb ("ships"). One term would read better.

No must-fix. S1 is open on this head and earns a delta review of its fix.

## Contract review brief — PR #38113 @ `d80d5fc3d7d49c3171d0c98159296276ab9fa74c` (card #37864)

`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template --paths packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #37864: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #38113: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `d80d5fc3d7d49c3171d0c98159296276ab9fa74c`
  · the check-runs on `d80d5fc3d7d49c3171d0c98159296276ab9fa74c`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/166e2125-4268-552f-a555-2b7c43a99f0f/scratchpad/pr-38113/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
     On every face, SQL push-down: a new id materialisation or in-app join where SQL could push down is a
     finding unless a reason is given (AGENTS.md, Prime Directive 5: SQL first).
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     Spell a must-fix or should-fix with its id and grade, `S1 (should-fix) — …`, and a clean round as
     `No must-fix, no should-fix.`: the queue guard reads a graded finding as OPEN on this head and
     refuses the record; the delta record names those it closes by id alone, `S1: closed`.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `620061105686dcfa58ddcfcd736bc534944b6bbe`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts + packages/runtime/src/domains/unavailable.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts, packages/types/src/server-fault-log.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/domain-501-language-37811.test.ts (the pin the catalog docblock cites)

Delta review of the fix for S1 of record 7232619079 (head `d80d5fc3`). Read: the diff `d80d5fc3..62006110` (two commits, `f80fc5ded` the fix and `620061105` a test import; 8 files; merge base unchanged at `93fa9118`), the claim amendment 7233430487 on card #37864 with the seat ruling "the fault log stays English", and the check-runs on this head. Everything the first record judged outside this delta stands as written there. The rest of the delta (`declared-capability-absence-warn-once.test.ts`, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Check-runs at the time of this record: 57 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed, 1 in progress (the `Test Core` aggregate; all ten `Test Core` legs, `Build Core`, `Type Check · workspace`, every `Test UI` leg, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `PR-body guards` have concluded success).

### ① Derived judgments

- `HttpDispatcherResult.response` gains the optional `faultLogMessage?: string`. `HttpDispatcherResult` is a published type (`packages/runtime/src/index.ts` re-exports it, and `@objectstack/adapter-hono` imports it), so this is a public-surface widening, and it is declared as one. Right: optional, additive, no existing producer or consumer has to change.
- The member never reaches the wire. Every writer of a dispatcher result at this head was read: `sendResultBase` writes `res.json(result.response.body)` and the status and headers only; the Hono adapter's `toResponse` writes `c.json(result.response.body, result.response.status)` and the headers only; `packages/verify` destructures `status` and `body`; the SSE branches read `result.result`, never `result.response`. The one place that hands a whole `response` object to a caller (`action-dispatch.ts`, `answer.response as ActionDispatchAnswer`) is the action door, which never calls `capabilityUnavailable`. Right.
- The operator's line: `capabilityUnavailable` sets `faultLogMessage` to `capabilityUnavailableMessage(slot)` with no locale, which is the English the first record showed equal to `serviceUnavailableMessage(slot)`; `sendResultBase` prints it when it is a string and the body's `error.message` otherwise, so every other answer logs exactly what it logged before. Right, and it is the ruling.
- zh-CN `capability_unavailable_ai` now says 「没有随附的实现」: a wording change in one locale, no key or placeholder moves. Right.

### ② Semver level

Changeset now lists `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/types`, all patch. Matches: an optional member on a published runtime type, a translation wording change, and a comment-only change in `types`. The added bullet (the fault log stays English) describes the tree.

Clause-②: yes (widening) — the changeset's line now names `HttpDispatcherResult.response.faultLogMessage` beside the five catalog keys; the PR body carries the same clause. Consistent with the diff. `Metadata-protocol: none` still holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Claim amendment 7233430487 covers the four added files (`http-dispatcher.ts`, `dispatcher-plugin.ts`, `server-fault-log.ts`, the warn-once test). Answered.
- For the seat, not graded: the PR body's "What changes", changeset line and "Size: 12 files" still describe the first head (the diff against `main` is now 16 files and three packages). The tree is what was judged.
- For the seat, not graded against this diff: the other localized catalog `501`s that went in with #37845 (`catalogNotImplemented` in the comment, webhook, approval, hook, auth and the remaining domain doors) set no `faultLogMessage`, so their once-per-route line still takes the first caller's language. They are on `main` already and outside this card's family; a follow-up card could set the English in `catalogNotImplemented` itself.
- SQL push-down: nothing in the delta touches a query. Nothing to flag.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts` — the three added docblock lines are true of the code: the family's line prints the English, through the answer's `faultLogMessage`. The claim is scoped to the `capability_unavailable_*` paragraph, where it holds.

`packages/runtime/src/domains/unavailable.ts` — the new paragraph agrees with the code below it; the answer is rebuilt by spread, so the `Vary` header and the body from `catalogNotImplemented` are kept.
